headline: Anthropic Shares Jump After Volatile First Week Since IPO
author: Carmen Reinicke

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- Anthropic PBC shares climbed above their $83 initial public offering price as the artificial intelligence lab looked to end its first calendar week on the Nasdaq after its record-setting debut on a positive note.

The stock increased about 11% from the previous session to $91.90 each as of 12:05 p.m. on Friday in New York, the highest intraday level since Monday, putting it on track to end a two-day streak of closing below the IPO price. Anthropic joined a broader rally in a shortened trading day following the Thanksgiving holiday, as risk appetite returned after a slump.

Concern over the pace of AI spending had roiled tech stocks in the lead-up to the Claude Code maker's record $119.5 billion first-time share sale, and spread to Anthropic's shares after Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang's return to the chipmaker as investors weighed the potential impact of the controversy on the AI ecosystem.

The trading gives the Dario Amodei-led company a market capitalization of roughly $1.7 trillion. That's below the peak of more than $2 trillion during the firm's debut on Nov. 19, when shares touched $115.10 before retreating.

The uneven debut has drawn scrutiny around the IPO's execution. Some investors have questioned the decision to allow Anthropic's underwriting banks to exercise the so-called over-allotment option after the first day, rather than preserving the ability to support the stock.

Others drew attention to the slug of as many as 315 million shares released from a lockup agreement on insiders on the first trading day, as part of the company's year-long staggered lockup releases, according to its prospectus.

A further tranche of as many as 303 million shares held by insiders are expected to become available for sale on Dec. 15, the prospectus shows. Also in December, indexes including the Nasdaq 100 could add Anthropic shares, leading to a wave of buying from tracking funds.

The rapid adoption of products such as Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent for software developers, and the company's revenue run rate of $81 billion at the end of October, made for a powerful sales pitch for the company's IPO. That helped investors overlook the company's committed spending nearing $901 billion through 2045.
